subject: Acme Retail — GPU pool starvation: interim update and follow-up
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-20T08:17:00-08:00
Subject: Acme Retail — GPU pool starvation: interim update and follow-up

Hi Sara / Acme ops team,

Quick update from Redwood: this morning between 06:12–07:04 PST your dedicated GPU pool experienced sustained queue growth that caused request latencies to exceed your SLA targets. We throttled new capacity-pinning operations and executed the pre-approved burst policy at 06:45 which reduced queue depth but did not fully restore nominal throughput.

What we did immediately:
- Enabled temporary burst nodes to add 12 GPUs (06:45)
- Disabled a misconfigured autoscaler policy that was delaying scale-ups for background jobs (06:58)
- Elevated priority for customer-facing inference traffic and applied prefix cache warmup for frequent models (07:10)

Current status: throughput is back to ~92% of expected at 08:10. We are continuing to monitor and have scheduled a controlled rolling capacity increase to reach full headroom by 12:00 PST.

Next steps we will deliver in the next 24 hours:
- Full incident timeline and root cause analysis (by EOD 1/20)
- Postmortem with action items and mitigations (by 1/21)
- Proposed customer credit calculation and a temporary QoS policy while we implement safeguards (by 1/21)

Attachments: saturation-timeline.pdf (timeline & metrics), capacity-mitigation-plan.md (planned config changes)

I know this impacted your peak traffic window — we take that seriously. I'll be on standby for whatever follow-ups you need; Marcus and Priyom are included for technical detail.

Best,
Naomi
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-20T08:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme Retail — GPU pool starvation: interim update and follow-up

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the fast response and the transparency. We saw elevated errors in our observability at 06:30 and had to fall back to cached responses for a subset of shoppers.

Two quick asks: can you confirm what the customer-facing impact window looks like (start/end) and whether our ingest pipeline needs any changes to avoid repeated throttling? Also please share the credit calc when you have it.

Sara
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Retail
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-20T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: quick tech summary and questions

Team — copying the internal tech notes here so we have a single record for postmortem drafting.

Observations:
- Root cause: autoscaler policy 1.3.7 was set with a min-backoff that prevented scale-up when concurrent background model warmups were queued; that collided with our fixed burst headroom threshold.
- Symptoms: queue depth spike at 06:12, increased token latency, some 503s when internal pre-warm jobs saturated N^ nodes.
- Temporary mitigation: manual disable of the failing policy + forced allocation of burst nodes.

Questions for follow-up:
1) Priyom — can you confirm whether the min-backoff change was rolled as part of the 1.3.7 deploy on 1/19?
2) Karthik — we should capture a short-run integration test for the autoscaler to surface this in canary. Can you add a checklist item to the canary runbook?

I'll start assembling the technical timeline for the postmortem doc.

-Marcus
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-20T13:42:00-08:00
Subject: Acme Retail — mitigation timeline, immediate config changes, and attachments

Sara — following up with the promised detail and attachments. Apologies again for the disruption. Below is the customer-facing timeline and the concrete config changes we'll apply during the maintenance window tonight (23:00–23:45 PST).

Customer-facing timeline (observed):
- 06:12 PST — queue growth begins; background warmups spike concurrent allocations
- 06:30 PST — first elevated 5xx rate observed in your telemetry (we flagged this to your ops)
- 06:45 PST — burst nodes allocated (12 GPUs) — partial relief
- 06:58 PST — autoscaler policy disabled manually — scale-up behavior restored
- 07:10 PST — priority routing + cache warmup applied — latency reduced to near normal

Planned config changes (tonight):
- Revert min-backoff to 30s for autoscaler (removes long delay before additional scale-up)
- Add a model-warmup isolation queue to prevent background jobs from starving production lanes
- Add workload-aware headroom: increase reserved headroom by 15% during your 05:00–09:00 peak window

Attachments included: saturation-timeline.pdf (detailed graphs), capacity-mitigation-plan.md (diff of config changes), credit-calculation.csv (proposed credit schedule).

We will run the maintenance during the 23:00–23:45 PST slot to avoid further impacts to your daytime traffic. Expect a full postmortem doc by 1/21 EOD. If you want an earlier call, I'm available at 15:00 PST.

Regards,
Naomi
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@acme-retail.com>, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-21T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Acme Retail — postmortem, customer credit, and long-term mitigations

Sara — attached is the final postmortem and our recommended fixes. Summary: the outage was caused by an autoscaler min-backoff regression introduced in release 1.3.7 (change set #8342) which prevented timely scale-ups when concurrent background warmups monopolized allocation slots. The immediate mitigations (burst nodes, policy disable, priority routing) restored service within ~58 minutes of the initial spike.

What we've shipped / scheduled:
- Hotfix: autoscaler min-backoff revert (deployed 1/20 23:12 PST)
- Isolation queue: implemented and live (1/21 02:04 PST) to separate background warmups from production lanes
- Peak headroom increase: active and monitored (1/21)
- Canary update: added a warmup-saturation scenario to our canary suite (in progress)

Customer impact and credits:
- Observed service degradation window: 06:12–07:10 PST (58 minutes)
- Proposed one-off credit: 8% of January usage billed to Acme Retail (see credit-calculation.csv)

Preventative action items (owner / ETA):
- Add autoscaler regression tests to CI (Priyom / 2 weeks)
- Canary scenario and runbook update (Karthik / 1 week)
- Telemetry alert tuning for background warmup anomalies (Marcus / 3 days)

Attachments: postmortem-final.pdf, credit-calculation.csv, remediation-checklist.md

We appreciate your patience — we will follow up with a short readout call if you’d like us to walk through the timeline and the credit calc.

Best,
Naomi
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
